requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: The `lengthof` predefined function has the signature lengthof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer.
requirements.original: lengthof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: The `lengthof` function SHALL return the length of a value or template of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, array or map.
requirements.original: This function returns the length of a value or template that is of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, array or map. The units of length for each

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: The units of length used by `lengthof` for each string type ARE the units defined in table 4.
requirements.original: charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, array or map. The units of length for each string type are defined in table 4 in the present document.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is of a record of or set of type
requirements.canonical: For a value or template of a record of or set of type, `lengthof` SHALL return the maximum of (a) the minimal length restriction value of the type, or 0 if the type has no minimal length restriction, and (b) the index of the last initialized element plus 1.
requirements.original: For values or templates of record `of or set` `of type, the value to be returned is the maximum of the minimal length` restriction value of the type, or 0 for types with no minimal length restriction, and the index of the last initialized element plus 1.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a map value
requirements.canonical: For a value of a map type, `lengthof` SHALL return the number of key value pairs in the map.
requirements.original: For values of the map type, the function returns the number of key value pairs in the map.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: the type of inpar is length restricted
requirements.canonical: For a length restricted string or list type, the length value returned by `lengthof` SHALL be at least the minimum length according to the type definition.
requirements.original: The length value returned in case of length restricted string or list type shall be at least the minimum length according to the type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is of a fixed length record of or set of type
requirements.canonical: The length returned by `lengthof` for a value of a fixed length record of or set of type IS always the fixed length according to the type definition.
requirements.original: In particular, the length of a fixed length record of or set of value will always be the fixed length according to the type definition.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is an array value or template
requirements.canonical: For an array value or template, `lengthof` SHALL return the fixed length of the corresponding record of type.
requirements.original: For array values or templates, the value to be returned is the fixed length of the corresponding record `of type.`

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: Because `in` formal parameters do not allow passing uninitialized values or templates, the `inpar` parameter of `lengthof` IS always at least partially initialized.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: As in formal parameters does not allow passing in uninitialized values or templates, even in these cases inpar will be at least partially initialized.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: The length of a universal charstring SHALL be calculated by counting each combining character and each hangul syllable character (including fillers) on its own.
requirements.original: The length of an universal charstring shall be calculated by counting each combining character and hangul syllable character (including fillers) on its own (see ISO/IEC 10646 [2], clauses 23 and 24).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a string-type template
requirements.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a string-type template, `inpar` SHALL only contain the matching mechanisms specific value, template list, complemented template list, pattern, "?" (AnyValue), "*" (AnyValueOrNone), combined template and the length restriction matching attribute.
requirements.original: When the function lengthof is applied to string-type templates, inpar shall only contain the following matching mechanisms: specific value, value list, complemented value list, pattern, "?" (AnyValue instead of value), "*" (AnyValueOrNone instead of value), combined template and the length restriction matching attribute.

ambiguity.issue: Clauses B.1.2.1 and B.1.2.2 name these matching mechanisms 'template list' and 'complemented template list'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a string-type template
requirements.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a string-type template, `inpar` SHALL match values of the same length only, with the exception of specific values and patterns.
requirements.original: In case of stringtype templates inpar shall match values of the same length only with the exception of specific values and patterns.

readings: A string-type template passed to lengthof SHALL match values of one length only, unless it is a specific value or a pattern, which MAY match values of different lengths.
A string-type template passed to lengthof SHALL match values of one length only; for specific values and patterns only the counting rule of clause 15.6.1 differs.
ambiguity.issue: It is unclear what the exception exempts; the examples ('1*F'H causes an error, '00*FF'O length(1..2) returns 2) suggest that patterns with '*' still need a determinable length. The first reading follows the wording and was chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a specific value or a pattern
requirements.canonical: For string-type templates that are specific values or patterns, `lengthof` SHALL return the number of indexable items according to the rules of clause 15.6.1.
requirements.original: In case of these two matching mechanisms, the lengthof function returns the number of indexable items according to the rules specified in clause 15.6.1.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a record of or set of template
requirements.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a template of a record of or set of type, `inpar` SHALL only contain the matching mechanisms specific value, template list, complemented template list, "?" (AnyValue), "*" (AnyValueOrNone), SuperSet, SubSet, combined template, permutation and the length restriction matching attribute.
requirements.original: When the function lengthof is applied to templates of record of or set of types, inpar shall only contain the following matching mechanisms: specific value, value list, complemented value list, "?" (AnyValue instead of value), "*" (AnyValueOrNone instead of value), SuperSet, SubSet, combined template, permutation and the length restriction matching attribute.

ambiguity.issue: Clauses B.1.2.1 and B.1.2.2 name these matching mechanisms 'template list' and 'complemented template list'.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a record of or set of template
requirements.canonical: When `lengthof` is applied to a template of a record of or set of type, `inpar` SHALL only match values for which `lengthof` gives the same result.
requirements.original: The parameter inpar shall only match values, for which the lengthof function would give the same result.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar contains uninitialized elements
requirements.canonical: Each uninitialized element contained in the `inpar` parameter of `lengthof` SHALL be counted as 1 element.
requirements.original: If inpar contains uninitialized elements, each of them shall be counted as 1 element, i.e. they shall be matched as if they contained the "?" (AnyElement inside value) matching character.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar contains uninitialized elements
requirements.canonical: Each uninitialized element contained in the `inpar` parameter of `lengthof` SHALL be matched as if it contained the "?" (AnyElement) matching mechanism.
requirements.original: If inpar contains uninitialized elements, each of them shall be counted as 1 element, i.e. they shall be matched as if they contained the "?" (AnyElement inside value) matching character.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: For record of, set of and array arguments, `lengthof` counts only the elements of the object passed as parameter; elements of nested types ARE NOT taken into account.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: In case of record ofs and set ofs and arrays only elements of the TTCN-3 object, which is the parameter of the function are calculated; i.e. no elements of nested types are taken into account when determining the return value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `lengthof` function in addition to its specific error causes.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a string-type template that can match values of different lengths
requirements.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with a string-type template that can match string values of different lengths SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: `inpar is a string-type template and it can match string values with different length or the length restriction` matching attribute contradicts the number of string elements in the template body;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: the length restriction contradicts the template body
requirements.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with a string-type template whose length restriction matching attribute contradicts the number of string elements in the template body SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: `inpar is a string-type template and it can match string values with different length or the length restriction` matching attribute contradicts the number of string elements in the template body;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is a record of or set of template that can match values of different lengths
requirements.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with a record of or set of template that can match values of different lengths SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: `inpar is a record of or set of type template and it can match values of different lengths or the length` restriction matching attribute contradicts the number of elements in the template body;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: the length restriction contradicts the template body
requirements.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with a record of or set of template whose length restriction matching attribute contradicts the number of elements in the template body SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: `inpar is a record of or set of type template and it can match values of different lengths or the length` restriction matching attribute contradicts the number of elements in the template body;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-lengthof
requirements.condition: inpar is not of one of the listed types
requirements.canonical: Calling `lengthof` with an argument that is not of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of or array SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: the template passed to the invalue parameter is not of type bitstring, hexstring, octetstring, charstring, universal charstring, record of, set of, or array.

readings: Calling lengthof with an argument not of a string, record of, set of, array or map type SHALL cause an error (map is allowed, as stated in C.2.1-s002/s006).
Calling lengthof with a map argument SHALL cause an error, because map is missing from the list.
ambiguity.issue: The error list omits map although lengthof is defined for maps; the first reading was chosen. The sentence also names the parameter 'invalue' instead of 'inpar'.

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.canonical: On real test systems, the length calculation of `inpar` CAN lead to an overflow problem that causes a compile time or runtime error.
requirements.original: NOTE 3: On real test systems the length calculation of inpar may lead to an overflow problem that causes compile time or runtime error.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.canonical: The `sizeof` predefined function has the signature sizeof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer.
requirements.original: sizeof(in template (present) any inpar) return integer

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.canonical: The `sizeof` function SHALL return the actual number of elements of a value or template of a record or set type.
requirements.original: This function returns the actual number of elements of a value or template of a record or set type (see note).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.canonical: The `sizeof` function MAY be applied to templates of record and set types.
requirements.original: The function sizeof is applicable to templates of record and set types.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.condition: inpar is a template
requirements.canonical: The `sizeof` function SHALL be applied to a template only if `sizeof` gives the same result on all values that match the template.
requirements.original: The function is applicable only if the sizeof function gives the same result on all values that match the template.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.canonical: `sizeof` counts only the elements of the object passed as parameter; elements of nested types or values ARE NOT taken into account.
requirements.original: NOTE: Only elements of the TTCN-3 object, which is the parameter of the function are calculated; i.e. no elements of nested types/values are taken into account at determining the return value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 apply to the `sizeof` function in addition to its specific error causes.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.condition: inpar is a template that can match values of different sizes
requirements.canonical: Calling `sizeof` with a template that can match values of different sizes SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: when inpar is a template and it can match values of different sizes;

requirements.subject: ent:fn-sizeof
requirements.condition: inpar is not of a record or set type
requirements.canonical: Calling `sizeof` with an argument that is not of a record or set type SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: the template passed to the inpar parameter is not of a record or set type.

ambiguity.issue: The error case names only 'the template', although sizeof also accepts values; the rule is read as applying to any argument.

non_requirement.reason: states that the overflow problem of NOTE 3 is out of scope
